items.name: storage.get
items.summary: Read a per-(user, App, key) JSON value from Anna Persistent Storage (APS). Returns the stored value plus an `etag` / `generation` for optimistic-concurrency writes, or `{value: null, exists: false}` if the key is absent. Soft-deleted and TTL-expired rows look the same as missing.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.storage.get(args: {key: string, scope?: 'app'|'user'|'tool', owner?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{value: any, etag?: string, generation?: number, exists: boolean}>

params.name: key
params.summary: Path-style key under the resolved `(scope, owner)` bucket. Must pass APS path validation (≤ 1024 chars total, ≤ 128 chars per `/`-separated segment, no leading `/`, no `.` / `..` segments, no control / bidi / zero-width chars).
notes: `HostRpcError("invalid_arg", "key required")` if missing / empty / non-string.
APS-backed handler additionally raises `invalid_path` from `validate_kv_key` when the key shape is illegal.
Keys are case-sensitive and not normalised — `foo/bar` and `Foo/bar` are different rows.
Use a stable prefix scheme (`notes/<id>`, `settings/preferences`) so `storage.list({prefix})` can page over related rows.

params.name: scope
params.summary: Visibility scope. `app` (default) reads the calling App's per-user bucket; `user` reads the user's cross-App bucket; `tool` is reserved (not yet exposed to iframes).
notes: `invalid_arg` if not one of `user` / `app` / `tool`.

PRIMARY gate: calling `storage.*` at all requires the method to be listed in `manifest.ui.host_api.storage` (e.g. `["get","set","delete","list"]`) — this is what `host_api_allows` checks. `manifest.permissions[]` is display/audit only and is NEVER consulted by the dispatcher.

The default `(scope=app, owner=self)` bucket needs NO further grant once `ui.host_api.storage` allows the method. Only NON-default scopes/owners require an extra `aps.scope.<scope>.<read|write>` (or `aps.scope.admin`) entry in `manifest.host_capabilities`.
Any non-default scope (e.g. `scope=user`) requires the manifest to declare `aps.scope.user.read` (or `aps.scope.admin`); the gate is enforced by `_check_storage_scope` *before* the handler runs.
`scope=tool` raises `not_implemented` today.

params.name: owner
params.summary: When `scope=app`, target a *different* App's bucket by slug. Defaults to `self` (calling App).
notes: Cross-owner reads (`scope=app` + `owner != self`) require `aps.scope.app.read` *with* cross-owner support; the host implementation currently raises `not_implemented` for cross-app reads.
Ignored for `scope=user` (the user bucket is owner-less by design).

returns.type: { value: any, etag?: string, generation?: number, exists: boolean }
returns.desc:
Hit: `{value, etag, generation, exists: true}`. Miss / expired / soft-deleted: `{value: null, exists: false}` (no `etag` / `generation`).

**The `exists` field is the source of truth.** A stored `null` value is indistinguishable from a missing key when you only inspect `value`. Always branch on `exists` for read-modify-write — see *executa-describe-result-shape.md*-style passthrough bugs where the SUCCESS path forgot to set `exists`, silently breaking append-to-list patterns.

`etag` is the opaque optimistic-concurrency token; pass it back as `if_match` on `set` / `delete` to guarantee in-place update. `generation` is a monotonic int (bumped on every set) — useful for ordering events from `runtime_state_synced`.

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `key` missing / empty / non-string, `scope` not in `user|app|tool`, or `limit` non-int (list).

errors.name: invalid_path
errors.desc: APS path validation rejected the key (too long, illegal segment, control chars, leading `/`).

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: Non-default `(scope, owner)` requested but manifest does not declare the matching `aps.scope.<scope>.<read>` (or `aps.scope.admin`) capability.

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Cross-owner `scope=app` reads or `scope=tool` — APS bridge has not yet wired this path.

errors.name: internal_error
errors.desc: DB / serialisation failure inside `StorageService.kv_get`.

limitations: Hot-path read: no per-call rate limit, but every miss still hits Postgres. Cache locally in the bundle if you poll on a timer.
TTL-expired rows are treated as missing on read but the underlying row may still consume bytes until the next GC sweep. `size_bytes` quota is released eagerly on `delete`.
`metadata` and `tags` are not returned by `get` (use `list` to project them).
Cross-owner reads (`scope=app`, `owner=<other-app>`) are still gated on a future implementation; today they raise `not_implemented` even when the manifest grants `aps.scope.app.read`.

items.name: storage.set
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → APS (Postgres) → quota reserve
items.summary: Write a JSON value under the resolved `(scope, owner, key)`. Idempotent in shape — upserts an existing row or creates a new one — but charges per-user `bytes_used` and `entry_count` quota on every call. Supports If-Match optimistic concurrency, metadata / tag annotations, and TTL-based auto-expiry.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.storage.set(args: {key: string, value: any, scope?: 'app'|'user'|'tool', owner?: string, if_match?: string, metadata?: object, tags?: string[], ttl_seconds?: number}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{etag: string, generation: number, size_bytes: number}>

params.name: key
params.summary: Same shape as `storage.get` — see the validation rules there.
notes: `invalid_arg` if missing / empty.
`invalid_path` from APS validator if illegal.

params.name: value
params.summary: Arbitrary JSON. Serialised via `json.dumps(default=str)` server-side so `datetime` / `Decimal` stringify automatically.
notes: There is no bundle-side size validator: the SDK does NOT pre-check `value`. Oversize payloads surface as `value_too_large` (APS per-row cap) or `state_too_large` (legacy backend 256 KiB) on the return path.
Functions, BigInts, and cyclic references are rejected at `postMessage` (V8 structured clone) — you never see them server-side.
Storing `null` is legal and round-trips correctly; consumers must branch on `cur.exists` to distinguish stored-null from absent.

params.name: if_match
params.summary: Optimistic-concurrency token from a prior `get` / `set` / `list` row. Pass to guarantee the row hasn't been touched by someone else since you observed it.
notes: `precondition_failed` if the token does not match the live row's `etag`, *including* when the row no longer exists (mirrors GCS / S3 If-Match semantics).
Concurrent first-insert races are also surfaced as `precondition_failed` — retry the read-modify-write loop and the second pass will hit the update branch.
Opaque; treat it as a black-box string. Format is `W/"<gen>-<digest>"` for the legacy backend and a payload hash for APS.

params.name: metadata
params.summary: Free-form annotation map. Not used for indexing; round-trips on `list`.
notes: Stored as JSON in `aps_entries.entry_metadata`.
Ignored by the legacy runtime_state backend.

params.name: tags
params.summary: Up to 32 free-form labels. Round-trips on `list` for client-side filtering; APS does not index by tag.
notes: Validated server-side by `KVSetRequest` (Pydantic) when used over the HTTP APS API; the iframe path forwards them verbatim.
Ignored by the legacy runtime_state backend.

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.summary: Auto-expire the row after N seconds (range 1..365 days). Expired rows look like 404 to `get` but bytes are reclaimed lazily by the GC sweep.
notes: Use for short-lived caches (session id, oauth state) rather than re-implementing TTL with timestamps in `value`.
Bound is server-side: `KVSetRequest.ttl_seconds` is `ge=1, le=60*60*24*365`.
Ignored by the legacy runtime_state backend.

params.name: scope
params.summary: Same as `storage.get`. Non-default scopes need `aps.scope.<scope>.write` in the manifest.
notes: Write action gate; `_check_storage_scope(manifest, 'set', args)` maps to `aps.scope.<scope>.write`.
Cross-owner writes (`scope=app`, `owner != self`) raise `not_implemented` today.

params.name: owner
params.summary: App slug to target (cross-app writes only). Defaults to the calling App.

returns.type: { etag: string, generation: number, size_bytes: number }
returns.desc:
Refreshed metadata for the just-written row.

• `etag` — feed into the next `if_match`. Bumps on every successful write even if `value` was identical.
• `generation` — monotonic int that survives `delete + recreate`? **No** — soft-delete then re-set creates a new row at `generation=1`. Treat it as a write-order indicator within a single live row, not a global change counter.
• `size_bytes` — serialised JSON length of the new value (used by the quota service).

**Side effect (legacy backend only):** an `anna.event.runtime_state_synced` is broadcast to the user's other windows with `{patch: {<key>: <value>}}`. The APS-backed handler does **not** emit this event today — apps that depend on live cross-tab sync should fall back to polling `storage.get` on focus.

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `key` missing / empty / non-string, or `scope` not in `user|app|tool`.

errors.name: invalid_path
errors.desc: APS path validation rejected the key shape.

errors.name: precondition_failed
errors.desc: `if_match` mismatch (including row missing or concurrent insert race).

errors.name: value_too_large
errors.desc: APS-backed handler: serialised `value` exceeds the per-row cap configured in `StorageService`.

errors.name: too_large
errors.desc: Legacy backend only: cumulative `window.runtime_state` would exceed **256 KiB** (`MAX_RUNTIME_STATE_BYTES`). Treat as the same class of failure as `value_too_large` from the app's perspective.

errors.name: quota_exceeded
errors.desc: Per-user APS byte / entry quota exhausted. Quota is reserved atomically (Redis Lua) before the row is written; failure rolls back.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: Non-default `(scope, owner)` without the matching `aps.scope.<scope>.write` (or `aps.scope.admin`) capability.

errors.name: forbidden_scope
errors.desc: APS service refused the scope (e.g. tool-level write without the corresponding entitlement).

errors.name: not_granted
errors.desc: User has not granted the App APS access at all (admin-level revoke).

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Cross-owner `scope=app` writes or `scope=tool`.

errors.name: rate_limited
errors.desc: Per-(user, App) write rate cap exceeded.

errors.name: internal_error
errors.desc: DB failure inside `StorageService.kv_set`.

limitations: **Quota is charged on every successful set**, not only on growth. Storing the same row repeatedly to refresh a timestamp will not blow the byte budget (delta is `new - old`) but it *does* contribute to write rate limits.
Legacy backend has a 256 KiB cumulative cap over **all** keys in `runtime_state`; APS has a per-row cap and a per-user total byte quota. Test both bounds if your bundle ships to both backends.
`runtime_state_synced` event is only emitted by the **legacy** backend. Apps that broadcast cross-window changes through this event will silently regress on the APS-backed prod path.
Soft-deleted rows are not visible to `get` but still hold `aps_entries` row IDs. Recreating with the same key allocates a fresh `generation=1` row.
`metadata` / `tags` are stored verbatim — no PII scrubbing. Do not stuff secrets into them; they leak via `list` to anything with read access.

items.name: storage.delete
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → APS (soft-delete + quota release)
items.summary: Remove a key from the resolved `(scope, owner)` bucket. The row is soft-deleted (kept for forensic / restore tooling) but immediately disappears from `get` / `list` and its bytes are returned to the per-user quota.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.storage.delete(args: {key: string, scope?: 'app'|'user'|'tool', owner?: string, if_match?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{deleted: true}>

params.name: key
params.summary: Same validation as `storage.get`.

params.name: if_match
params.summary: Optimistic-concurrency token. Pass to guarantee you delete the exact row you observed (e.g. avoid clobbering a re-created entry under the same key).
notes: `precondition_failed` if the etag does not match the live row.
Ignored by the legacy backend (which has no per-row etag).

params.name: scope
params.summary: Same gating as `storage.set` (`action='write'` → needs `aps.scope.<scope>.write`).

params.name: owner
params.summary: Cross-app delete target slug. Defaults to self.

returns.desc:
Always `{deleted: true}` on success. The legacy backend returns `{ok: true}` instead; treat both shapes as equivalent.

**Quota is released eagerly**: `kv_delete` calls `_reserve_quota(..., -size)` to give the bytes back before the transaction commits. Subsequent `set` calls see the reclaimed headroom immediately.

**Side effect (legacy backend only):** broadcasts `runtime_state_synced` with `{patch: {<key>: null}}` — apps relying on this for cross-tab sync will not receive it on the APS-backed prod path.

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `key` missing / empty / non-string.

errors.name: not_found
errors.desc: Key does not exist (APS backend only — the legacy backend silently no-ops a missing key).

errors.name: precondition_failed
errors.desc: `if_match` etag mismatch.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: Non-default scope without `aps.scope.<scope>.write`.

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Cross-owner `scope=app` or `scope=tool`.

limitations: Soft-delete only: the row is hidden from `get` / `list` but persisted in `aps_entries`. There is no public `restore` API today.
Legacy backend silently succeeds when the key is missing (returns `{ok: true}`); APS backend raises `not_found`. Treat the call as best-effort and swallow `not_found` if you do not need it.
`if_match` is ignored on the legacy backend — concurrent deletes from another tab will not be surfaced.
Bulk delete is not exposed. Iterate `storage.list({prefix})` + `storage.delete({key})` per row.

items.name: storage.list
items.since: anna-app-runtime v0.1 · `metadata` / `tags` returned since APS Phase 4
items.summary: Enumerate keys in the resolved `(scope, owner)` bucket whose path starts with `prefix`. Returns metadata-only rows (no `value` — call `storage.get(key)` per item if you need the payload). Paginated by an opaque `cursor`.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.storage.list(args?: {prefix?: string, cursor?: string, limit?: number, scope?: 'app'|'user'|'tool', owner?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{items: Array<{key: string, etag: string, size_bytes: number, metadata: object|null, tags: string[]|null, updated_at: string|null}>, next_cursor: string|null}>

params.name: prefix
params.summary: Path-prefix filter. Empty string lists the whole bucket.
notes: May end with `/` (matches a directory-style prefix) and may include empty trailing segments (`a/` is legal).
Otherwise follows the same validation as `key` — `..` segments, control chars, and absolute paths are rejected with `invalid_path`.
Match is plain `startswith` — there is no glob, no regex, no SQL `LIKE` wildcard escaping required from the caller (the service does it internally).

params.name: cursor
params.summary: Opaque pagination cursor returned by a prior `list` call as `next_cursor`.
notes: Encodes the last seen key (base64-ish); not stable across schema changes. Always re-paginate from the start when retrying.
Passing a stale cursor returns rows that sort after it — may legitimately yield zero items if the bucket was drained.
Legacy backend uses the raw key as the cursor (no encoding); APS encodes it.

params.name: limit
params.summary: Page size, 1..1000. Default 100.
notes: `invalid_arg` if non-int.
Values ≤ 0 or > 1000 raise `invalid_arg` on the legacy backend; the APS backend clamps silently via `max(1, min(limit, LIST_MAX_LIMIT))`.

params.name: scope
params.summary: Non-default scopes need `aps.scope.<scope>.read`.

params.name: owner
params.summary: Cross-app listing target. Defaults to self.

returns.type: { items: Array<{key, etag, size_bytes, metadata, tags, updated_at}>, next_cursor: string | null }
returns.desc:
Pageful of row heads, sorted ascending by `key`.

• `items[].metadata` / `items[].tags` are populated from `aps_entries` (APS backend) and are `null` on the legacy backend (which has no metadata column).
• `items[].updated_at` is an ISO-8601 string on the APS backend; `null` on the legacy backend.
• `next_cursor: null` means "no more pages"; otherwise feed it back as `cursor` on the next call.

**Soft-deleted and TTL-expired rows are excluded.** Listing is consistent with `get` — if a key shows up here, a subsequent `get` will return `exists: true` (modulo races).

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `limit` is non-int, or `limit ≤ 0` / `limit > 1000` on the legacy backend.

errors.name: invalid_path
errors.desc: `prefix` longer than 1024 chars, absolute, or contains forbidden segments.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: Non-default scope without `aps.scope.<scope>.read`.

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Cross-owner `scope=app` listings or `scope=tool`.

limitations: Metadata-only — does NOT return `value`. Apps that need bulk reads must `list` then `get` per key (no batch endpoint exists today).
No filtering by `metadata` / `tags` — they are returned for client-side projection only. APS has no tag index.
Cursor is opaque and **not stable** across deploys: do not persist it across sessions. Re-paginate from start on cold load.
Legacy backend can be slow on large buckets (it sorts the entire dict in memory); the APS backend uses an indexed `LIKE 'prefix%'` scan.
Order is byte-wise ascending on the raw `key` string — Unicode is collated by codepoint, not locale.
